chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I mention the name of Allah over food?' He said, 'If the vessels differ, mention the name over each vessel.' I said, 'And if I forget?' He said, 'Say: In the name of Allah over its first and its last.'

key_terms.أوله وآخراه: Its first and its last (referring to the sequence of eating)
key_terms.تسمية: Mentioning the name of Allah (tasmiyah) before eating

ai.seo_question: How to handle tasmiyah when eating from multiple dishes or forgetting to say Bismillah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when dining from multiple distinct vessels, one must recite the tasmiyah individually for each to ensure proper sanctification of every portion. In cases of forgetfulness, the remedy of saying 'Bismillah' over the first and last vessel serves as a comprehensive covering (istighraq) for the intermediate items, reflecting the juristic principle of generalization in ritual recitations. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise ritual etiquette (adab) during daily acts of worship, linking physical sustenance to spiritual mindfulness.
